name: 001_default_print_no_expression.sh
exercises: Default action when no expression is given
expected: Starting point and its descendants are printed (default -print)
manpage_quote: If no expression is given, the expression -print is used (but you should probably consider using -print0 instead, anyway).

name: 002_no_starting_point_dot.sh
exercises: Default starting point when none is given
expected: find treats '.' as the start point; paths printed are relative to '.'
manpage_quote: If no starting-point is specified, `.' is assumed.

name: 003_maxdepth_0_startpoint_only.sh
exercises: -maxdepth 0 boundary
expected: Only the starting point itself is processed; no descent
manpage_quote: Using -maxdepth 0 means only apply the tests and actions to the starting-points themselves.

name: 004_maxdepth_1_boundary.sh
exercises: -maxdepth 1 boundary (one level vs two)
expected: Start point and immediate children only; grandchildren excluded
manpage_quote: Descend at most levels (a non-negative integer) levels of directories below the starting-points.

name: 005_mindepth_1_excludes_start.sh
exercises: -mindepth 1 boundary
expected: All files except the starting point are processed
manpage_quote: Using -mindepth 1 means process all files except the starting-points.

name: 006_name_basename_not_path.sh
exercises: -name matches base name only; a pattern with a slash never matches
expected: -name 'dir/target' matches nothing even though that path exists
manpage_quote: Base of file name (the path with the leading directories removed) matches shell pattern pattern.  Because the leading directories of the file names are removed, the pattern should not include a slash, because `-name a/b' will never match anything (and you probably want to use -path instead).

name: 007_iname_case_insensitive.sh
exercises: -iname case-insensitive globbing (vs case-sensitive -name)
expected: -iname 'fo*' matches the file 'Foo'
manpage_quote: Like -name, but the match is case insensitive.  For example, the patterns `fo*' and `F??' match the file names `Foo', `FOO', `foo', `fOo', etc.

name: 008_name_leading_dot_matched.sh
exercises: Glob metacharacter matches a leading dot (PASC interpretation 126)
expected: -name '*hidden' matches the dotfile '.hidden'
manpage_quote: As of findutils-4.2.2, shell metacharacters (`*', `?' or `[]' for example) used in filename patterns match a leading `.', because IEEE POSIX interpretation 126 requires this.

name: 009_type_comma_list.sh
exercises: -type comma-separated list (GNU extension) matches the union
expected: -type f,l matches the regular file and the symlink, not the directory
manpage_quote: To search for more than one type at once, you can supply the combined list of type letters separated by a comma `,' (GNU extension).

name: 010_size_rounding_up.sh
exercises: -size rounds up to the next unit; -size -1M matches only empty files
expected: -size -1M matches the 0-byte file but not the 1-byte file
manpage_quote: Therefore -size -1M is not equivalent to -size -1048576c.  The former only matches empty files, the latter matches files from 0 to 1,048,575 bytes.

name: 011_size_exact_c_no_match.sh
exercises: -size exact byte count; n does not match n-1
expected: -size 5c matches the 5-byte file, not the 4-byte file
manpage_quote: The + and - prefixes signify greater than and less than, as usual; i.e., an exact size of n units does not match.

name: 012_empty_regular_and_dir.sh
exercises: -empty matches empty regular files and empty directories
expected: Empty file and empty dir match; non-empty file and non-empty dir do not
manpage_quote: File is empty and is either a regular file or a directory.

name: 013_a_higher_precedence_than_o.sh
exercises: -a binds tighter than -o (documented precedence surprise)
expected: '-name afile -o -name bfile -print' prints only bfile, never afile
manpage_quote: The command find . -name afile -o -name bfile -print will never print afile because this is actually equivalent to find . -name afile -o \( -name bfile -a -print \).  Remember that the precedence of -a is higher than that of -o and when there is no operator specified between tests, -a is assumed.

name: 014_explicit_action_suppresses_default_print.sh
exercises: An explicit action (other than -prune/-quit) inhibits default -print
expected: With -fprint present, nothing is written to stdout
manpage_quote: The -print action is performed on all files for which the whole expression is true, unless it contains an action other than -prune or -quit.  Actions which inhibit the default -print are -delete, -exec, -execdir, -ok, -okdir, -fls, -fprint, -fprintf, -ls, -print and -printf.

name: 015_prune_skips_subtree.sh
exercises: -prune prevents descent into a matched directory (-path ... -prune -o -print idiom)
expected: Contents of the pruned directory are not printed; other files are
manpage_quote: True; if the file is a directory, do not descend into it.  If -depth is given, then -prune has no effect.

name: 016_print_quit_stops_early.sh
exercises: -quit stops find immediately after the current file
expected: With two start points and '-print -quit', only the first is printed
manpage_quote: After -quit is executed, no more files specified on the command line will be processed.  For example, `find /tmp/foo /tmp/bar -print -quit` will print only `/tmp/foo`.

name: 017_not_negates_test.sh
exercises: ! / -not logical negation of a test
expected: '! -type d' selects the regular file, not the directory
manpage_quote: ! expr True if expr is false.

name: 018_nonexistent_start_path_errors.sh
exercises: Nonexistent starting point is an error
expected: find exits with nonzero status
manpage_quote: find exits with status 0 if all files are processed successfully, greater than 0 if errors occur.

name: 019_newerxy_invalid_combo_errors.sh
exercises: -newerXY with X=t is an invalid combination
expected: find exits with a fatal (nonzero) status
manpage_quote: Some combinations are invalid; for example, it is invalid for X to be t.  Some combinations are not implemented on all systems; for example B is not supported on all systems.  If an invalid or unsupported combination of XY is specified, a fatal error results.

name: 020_delete_nonempty_dir_errors.sh
exercises: -delete on a non-empty directory fails
expected: find's exit status is nonzero
manpage_quote: The -delete action will fail to remove a directory unless it is empty.

name: 021_files0from_and_cmdline_start_errors.sh
exercises: -files0-from is mutually exclusive with command-line start points
expected: find exits with nonzero status
manpage_quote: Using this option and passing starting points on the command line is mutually exclusive, and is therefore not allowed at the same time.

name: 022_path_matches_whole_name.sh
exercises: -path matches the whole name; wildcards span '/' (not treated specially)
expected: -path '<start>/sr*sc' matches '<start>/src/misc'
manpage_quote:
File name matches shell pattern pattern.  The metacharacters do not treat `/' or `.' specially; so, for example,
                  find . -path "./sr*sc"
       will print an entry for a directory called ./src/misc (if one exists).
